stories.title: Unification ministry's 2027 budget plan seeks to revive railway project
stories.summary: The unification ministry is seeking over 1.25 trillion won (US$913.7 million) for next year's budget, including 1.11 trillion won earmarked for the "inter-Korean cooperation fund," it said Tuesday, amid efforts to revive long-dormant exchanges with North Korea. The ministry's budget proposal marks a 0.82 percent increase from this year, and will top 1 trillion won for a second consecutive year, if approved by the National Assembly. Among the notable items is roughly 24.7 billion won for an envisioned cross-border railway, named Gyeongwon Railway, which the government plans to resume next year. Work on the line was halted in May 2016, following North Korea's fourth nuclear test earlier that year. The ministry aims to finish the South Korean section by 2029. Once completed, the railway would connect Seoul and Wonsan in the North. Funding for a North Korean human rights foundation was slashed by 90 percent because the organization has yet to launch. According to a unification ministry official, the cut simply reflects that all allocated funds from last year went entirely unused. Reflecting a shift in policy priorities, the ministry's next-year budget prioritizes youth education on "peaceful coexistence," a campaign that marks a departure from previous governments' focus on unification. To that end, some 7.15 billion won will be set aside to build up a dedicated workforce of up to 10,000 people. The ministry has hired around 4,000 so far, it said. Funding for humanitarian aid, including support for infants and healthcare and relief assistance, is set to be cut by 15 percent after an evaluation flagged related programs as underperforming.

stories.title: Kākāpō rising: 90 chicks swell population of the world’s heaviest parrot
stories.summary: Critically endangered New Zealand bird enjoys record breeding season triggered by mass fruiting of native tree, pushing its numbers to 325 The population of the world’s heaviest parrot, the kākāpō , has surpassed 300 birds for the first time in 75 years, after a record breeding season triggered by the mass fruiting of a native New Zealand tree. Ninety chicks were officially added to the population of the critically endangered birds on 1 September, pushing the total to 325 – a record high since recovery efforts began. Continue reading...

stories.title: Ukraine unable to intercept new models of Russia’s Geran drones — newspaper
stories.summary: LONDON, September 1. Ukraine is facing difficulties intercepting new models of Russia’s Geran drones, The Guardian reported. According to the newspaper, the new-model drones have a cruising speed of about 400 kilometers per hour, roughly twice that of the piston-engine version, making them extremely difficult for Ukraine to intercept. The paper added that Russia had begun manufacturing and deploying its latest jet-powered drones in significant numbers in the spring.

stories.title: Trump wins Supreme Court ruling to continue White House ballroom construction
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Donald Trump to continue construction of his White House ballroom, granting him a major victory as he works to leave a permanent mark on Washington. The conservative-dominated court ruled 5-4 to lift a lower order demanding most construction be halted, saying that the plaintiff in the case likely did not have legal standing to sue.
